clue.text: Possible source of "real nerds'?

indicators.note: the answer's letters are a possible source from which the quoted phrase can be rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who first called a group of people real nerds.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the letters of REAL NERDS gives the answer, and someone who calls people real nerds is just the sort to be its source.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads insulting remarks about others is a likely origin of a jibe such as this one.

clue.text: Temporarily dismiss rugby player

definitions.meaning: to lay off workers for a while
the fly-half position in rugby union, playing just behind the scrum

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to lay off temporarily, and in rugby union the term names the fly-half.

clue.text: Story-teller producing a work about English Society

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first pieces surround the next ones

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A writer of tales produces a book about English high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist is the archetypal teller of moral stories about animals.

clue.text: One who won't conform troubled residents

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are disturbed and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A nonconformist has upset the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter disagrees with the established church or opinion and refuses to comply with it.

clue.text: Conflict arises over Kent town getting harsh treatment

indicators.note: arises in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: war is armed conflict
Deal is a coastal town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out in a Kentish town and residents are treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply places the reversed piece above DEAL in the down entry. DEAL is a seaside town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for unfair or unkind handling of someone.

clue.text: Social class, with the French, causes continuous irritation

parts.note: rank means social standing or class
les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: Class distinctions, along with the French, are a constant source of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To fester or keep annoying someone persistently, like a grievance that will not heal.

clue.text: On a drinking session

parts.note: a bout is a spell of heavy drinking

explanation.surface: Someone is out on a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean concerning, as in a book on or regarding birds.

clue.text: Greek story for Americans

definitions.meaning: relating to Athens and its classical dialect
American spelling of storey, a level of a building, here the top one under the roof

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes ancient Athenian things, and also names the loft room, the uppermost floor of a house.

clue.text: Work with journalists their boss tyrannised

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
the press means journalists collectively
ED, short for editor, is the head of the journalists

explanation.surface: A newspaper staff complain that their chief bullied them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled over cruelly or unjustly is a synonym for being kept down by force.

clue.text: Story about vacuous twit is gossip

indicators.note: about means the story goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the first and last letters of twit remain

explanation.surface: A tale about an empty-headed fool spreads as rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter or telling tales about others is a synonym for tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Judge stopping short those who are foolish

indicators.note: stopping short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: to assess is to judge or evaluate

explanation.surface: A judge cuts short the arguments of silly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are proverbially stupid, so the plural is used for fools.

clue.text: Tried a snooker shot but showed decline in form

definitions.meaning: attempted to sink a ball into a pocket in snooker
an idiom meaning deteriorated badly or was ruined

explanation.definitionFit: Literally attempting to pocket a ball in snooker, and idiomatically falling apart or going to ruin.

clue.text: Exhaust to get rid of when there's parking inside

indicators.note: inside says the parking letter goes within the other word

parts.note: to delete is to remove or get rid of
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A driver tries to dispose of exhaust fumes in a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up or drain completely, as in exhausting supplies.

clue.text: Milky, sticky stuff served with duck

parts.note: lac is a resinous substance secreted by insects
a teal is a small freshwater duck

explanation.surface: A white, gooey sauce is served with duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to milk or resembles it in colour and consistency.

clue.text: Excellent appointment on which HM's authority is stamped?

definitions.text: on which HM's authority is stamped?
definitions.meaning: mail bearing the monarch's head on its stamp, sent by the faster Royal Mail service

explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her (or His) Majesty, whose head appears on British stamps; the Royal Mail offers a faster priority grade of letter delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A top job is a superior position, and the speedier grade of British mail carries the royal head on its stamp.

clue.text: Where one may ride across bay, say, having unpleasant boat-trip .

definitions.text: Where one may ride across bay, say

parts.note: rotten means nasty or unpleasant
a row is an outing in a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A rider on a bay horse also endures a miserable outing in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bay is a reddish-brown horse. This is the famous sandy bridle track in London's Hyde Park, where riders exercise horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The London park track is a well-known place for horse riding, and a bay is a horse.

clue.text: Given freedom at bottom of page, nothing new to say

indicators.note: at bottom of places the freedom word below the page letter in this down entry

parts.note: latitude means scope or freedom of action

explanation.surface: Someone granted freedom at the foot of a page finds they have nothing original to write.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused remark offers nothing original, which is what a banal saying is.

clue.text: One who's touched up at work?

definitions.text: One who's touched up at work?

parts.words: One who's touched up at work?
parts.note: suggests a harassed employee, but means someone whose job is retouching old paintings and furniture

explanation.definitionFit: An art conservator's job is retouching damaged pictures to bring them back to their original state.

clue.text: Crank beginning run

parts.note: starting means beginning
to handle a business is to run or manage it

explanation.surface: An eccentric is about to start running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' looks like an eccentric person; it is the lever once used to turn an engine over by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cars were started with a hand crank inserted at the front of the engine.

clue.text: Popular person in court king accepted as policy-maker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: accepted means the king letter is taken inside the court word

parts.note: a suer is someone who brings a lawsuit
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A well-liked litigant takes on a king's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policy-maker' suggests a politician; here the policy is an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance company writes out cover documents, so it is literally the one who issues policies.

clue.text: Escape? Come off it!

definitions.meaning: a flight from a crime scene
an exclamation of disbelief, meaning surely not

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a fugitive's flight; spoken as two words it is an exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Piece of land has walk going round river and lake

indicators.note: going round means the walk word encircles the river letter

parts.note: to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: A plot of ground includes a footpath circling a river and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot or tract of ground, as in a parcel of real estate.

clue.text: A planet without river or lake — hellish frontier

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the planet goes round the river letter

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun

explanation.surface: A planet lacking any rivers or lakes would be a hellish place to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside. The answer is the volcanic lake near Naples that the Romans held to be the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth this crater lake in Campania was the gateway to the underworld.

clue.text: Name a place that's beastly and disagreeable

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs, a home for beasts

explanation.surface: Someone names a filthy, unpleasant spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant or offensive is a synonym for horrid.

clue.text: Lady's outfit badly sewn — it split, finally

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly and reshuffled
finally picks out the closing letter of split

explanation.surface: A woman's clothes were poorly stitched and came apart at the seams.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching cardigan and jumper worn together is a classic women's ensemble.

clue.text: Australian craft — bum-boats?

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Australia
bot is British slang for the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Australian vessels are named for one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boats?' adds a nod to the other sense: a wooden clog, since big shoes are called boats in slang. In Australia it also names a small sailing dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: A small single-handed sailing dinghy goes by this name, notably in Australia.

clue.text: One may often be seen twisting at a party

definitions.text: One may often be seen twisting at a party

parts.words: One may often be seen twisting at a party
parts.note: suggests a dancer doing the twist, but means a spiral tool turned to open wine bottles

explanation.definitionFit: A spiral bottle opener is twisted into the stopper of wine bottles opened at celebrations.

clue.text: Brown northern river, the source of which is hidden

indicators.text: the source of which is hidden
indicators.note: the source of a river is its start, so the first letter is concealed and dropped

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary in northern England

explanation.surface: A muddy northern river rises from an unseen spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The HUMBER is the estuary in north-east England that divides Yorkshire from Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural earth pigment of a dark brownish shade.

clue.text: Blue lines artist produced

parts.note: low means sad or blue
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A depressed painter produced some drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial scenes with matchstick figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancashire painter is famous for his industrial townscapes with thin figures.

clue.text: One can't make anything go with orange

definitions.text: One can't make anything go with orange

parts.words: One can't make anything go with orange
parts.note: suggests a fashion or decor problem, but refers to a versifier, since famously no English word chimes with orange

explanation.definitionFit: A writer of verse, especially a poor one, struggles to find a word matching the sound of orange.
